events.text: The Faculty Senate has voted 31–2 to express 'grave concern' about the parking situation. It is unclear what they would like you to do, and neither of the two dissenters can be located.
A section of roof has come off {building} in the night. Facilities has cordoned off the quad beneath it and described the timber, in writing, as 'no longer load-bearing in the usual sense'.
Students in the overflow rooms have written a joint letter. It is polite, it is numbered, and it has been copied to the local paper.
The Committee on Committee Reform has reported. Its principal recommendation is the establishment of a standing subcommittee to monitor implementation.

choices.label: Thank the committee and dissolve it

events.text: An alumna of the {class} has left the college $1.2M, on the single condition that it never be spent on administration. Her solicitor was firm about this and appears to have enjoyed saying it.
{faculty} has an offer from a college with a larger endowment and a worse library. They have brought you the letter, which is either a courtesy or an opening bid.
The heating has failed across the older buildings in the third week of a cold term. Students are attending lectures in coats and have begun, inevitably, to enjoy it.
A student of {program} has won a national prize, and the local paper has run the photograph large. The department is behaving as though it planned this.
The auditors have asked, in a footnote, whether the college's reserves policy is 'documented anywhere'. It is not, and writing one down now would mean writing down what it has been.

choices.label: Undertake to review it next year

events.title: The storm
events.text:
The storm came through on the Tuesday night and took the roofs off two buildings, a run of mature limes along the north walk, and the temporary structure nobody had got round to making permanent. Nobody was hurt. The engineers' report is nine pages long and uses the word 'char' as a verb, which the insurers have queried.

The college has been here before and the minutes say so: in the founder's time the same wind took the chapel and the response, recorded with some satisfaction, was to build it back higher.

choices.label: Make safe and defer the rest
Launch a storm appeal
choices.note: The alumni are asked, and remember being asked

events.title: The markets
events.text:
The markets have done in a fortnight what they usually take a decade to do. The endowment is worth materially less than it was at breakfast on the Monday, the investment committee has asked for a special meeting, and three members of it have separately telephoned to say they were always uneasy about the allocation.

None of this changes what the college costs to run this year. That is the whole of the problem.

choices.label: Ride it out on the standing draw
Cut this year's spending to match

events.text: The inspector has condemned the boiler in {building} and left a notice on it in a colour the college has not seen before. The plant room has been locked and the key is with Facilities, who would like it on record that they have mentioned the boiler twice.

The surveyor's report on {building} notes, in passing, that the ivy on the west face is now doing some of the work the west face used to do. The Alumni Office has asked whether the ivy could be considered for listing.

choices.label: Leave the ivy where it is

events.text: Slates have been coming off {building} in ones and twos for a month. Nobody has been hit. The Head of Facilities has begun describing this as the college's good fortune rather than its policy.

The town has written about {building}. The letter is courteous for two paragraphs and then uses the word 'eyesore', which the Clerk has underlined. A photograph is enclosed, taken from the road, in the rain.

choices.label: Hoarding and a sign about future plans

events.text: The refurbishment survey of {building} has found asbestos in the ceiling voids, the pipe lagging and, unexpectedly, the stage curtain of the lecture theatre. Work has stopped. The contractor is being very calm about it, which is worse.
The basement of {building} took nine inches of water in the night. The archive was on the floor because the shelving was ordered in a year the shelving budget did not survive.
The bell mechanism has stopped. It stopped once before, in the founder's time, and the minute recording the repair is the only document in the archive with an exclamation mark in it.

choices.label: Fit a recording and a timer

events.text: Disease has been confirmed in the elms along the main walk. The recommendation is to fell the affected trees this winter and the ones either side of them as a precaution, which is most of the walk.

A brown line now runs corner to corner across the quad, worn by everyone who has ever been late. Grounds have reseeded it twice. The Bursar has suggested, not entirely as a joke, that the college pave what the students have surveyed for it.

choices.label: Rail it off and reseed
choices.note: $12k, and they will go round it or they will not

events.text: A class that has kept in touch with each other more than with {school} would like to give it three hundred trees. There is no money attached. There is a planting plan, drawn by one of them, and it is rather good.

choices.label: Thank them and decline the planting

events.text: The rating agency has asked for a meeting about the construction borrowing. The questions sent in advance are all reasonable, which is what the Bursar finds alarming about them.

choices.label: Present the case and hold the debt
choices.note: Free; they will want the meeting again

events.text: The bank has written about the operating account. The letter uses the phrase 'in the ordinary course' four times and means the opposite of it.

choices.label: Draw on the endowment to cover it
Arrange a facility
choices.note: Fees, and the board hears about it

events.text: The auditors intend to qualify their opinion on the year. They have offered to discuss the wording, which is a kindness, and to do so at the Audit Committee, which is not.

choices.label: Contest the treatment
choices.note: $40k in advice, and a longer meeting

events.text: The fund has outgrown the arrangement it was set up with in the founder's time, which was a local firm, a handshake, and a quarterly lunch. The local firm is aware of this and has been gracious.

A bequest has arrived with conditions: the money is for a building, the building is to bear the donor's name, and the name is to appear 'in stone, not in vinyl'. The sum is substantial. The estate's solicitors have used the word 'exacting' about the family.

choices.label: Ask for the conditions to be loosened
Decline the bequest
choices.note: Nothing, and a letter to write

events.text: The Finance Committee has noticed the draw. One member has prepared a chart showing what the fund would be worth in thirty years at the current rate and has brought copies, which is the part the Bursar objects to.

choices.label: Cut the draw and find the money elsewhere

events.text: The hiring freeze has held for three years. The post that opened when {faculty} took leave has been advertised, unadvertised and advertised again, and the department has stopped asking about it.
A trustee has resigned. The letter gives pressure of work as the reason and is three lines long, which is two lines longer than it needed to be and one line shorter than a letter that meant it.

choices.label: Leave the seat open for now
choices.note: Free, and the board notices the chair

events.text: A reporter has been asking the kind of questions that mean they already have the figures. The deadline is Friday. The Communications Officer would like to know what the college's position is, and does not appear to be joking.

choices.label: Give them the numbers and a statement
choices.note: Free; it is worse for a day

choices.label: Decline to comment
choices.note: Free; it is worse for a month

events.text: The board would like a retreat. The proposal is for two days at a hotel with a facilitator, and the stated purpose is to think strategically about the next twenty years, which the last retreat also did.

choices.label: One day, in the library, no facilitator

events.text: A tenure case has reached the President's desk. The department is for it, the school's committee is against it, and the external letter praises the candidate's work at length before declining to recommend anything at all.

choices.label: Grant tenure
choices.note: A career, and a salary line forever

choices.label: Deny, with a year to find something

events.text: {faculty} has not come back from sabbatical. The work is going well, apparently, and there has been a letter about extending, and the teaching that was covered for one year has now been covered for two.

choices.label: Extend the leave
choices.note: $90k in cover; the book may be good

choices.label: Require a return or a resignation

events.text: {faculty}, the best appointment {school} has made in years, has a spouse who is also an academic, in a field the college does not teach, and has asked whether anything might be possible. Two other institutions have already said that something might be.

choices.label: Fund a teaching line for the spouse
choices.note: $130k a year; the college keeps both

events.text: Four emeritus professors are using offices the departments would like back. None of them teaches. All of them are in most days. One of them is the reason two of the others came here at all.

choices.label: Leave them where they are
choices.note: $40k a year in space nobody counts

choices.label: Move them to a shared room
choices.note: Free, and it will be mentioned at every reunion

events.text: The seminar that was capped at fifteen has thirty-one in it. The instructor has divided them into two groups meeting fortnightly, which is a solution, and has written to ask whether it is the college's solution.

choices.label: Cover it with teaching by the course
Raise the cap and say so plainly

events.text: {faculty}'s lectures have started attracting people who are not registered for them, including, twice, members of the public. The lecture theatre holds ninety. The Fire Officer has been in touch.

choices.label: Move it and open it to the town

events.text: The teaching returns are the worst the college has recorded. The written comments are not angry, which the Dean has noted as the concerning part; they are patient, and several of them say that the students had expected this.

choices.label: Fund a teaching programme and protect the time
Note the returns and circulate them

events.text: The accreditation panel will visit in the spring. The self-study runs to a hundred and forty pages, and the covering letter asks for evidence of 'continuous improvement', which the Registrar has spent a week trying to write honestly.

Enrolment in {program} is down for the fourth year. The department's case for keeping it is that it is the kind of thing a university should teach, which is true, and that it will recover, which is where the case becomes thinner.

choices.label: Fund it properly and give it three years
Teach out the students in it and close it
choices.note: Saves the line; somebody will write to the paper

events.text: {school} has buildings, a seal, a bell and no programmes. The Registrar has drafted a letter to prospective students and has got as far as the second paragraph before the difficulty became structural.

choices.label: Wait until it can be done properly
choices.note: Free, and another year goes by

events.text: A private library is coming up: eleven thousand volumes, a working collection rather than a beautiful one, from a scholar who taught here briefly and disliked it. The heirs would prefer it went somewhere it would be used.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.note: Free; it goes to a university with more shelves

events.text: Forty students are sitting in the foyer of {building}. They have a list of six things, four of which the college agrees with, and they have been letting the cleaners through since Tuesday.

choices.label: Meet them and concede what is fair
Wait them out
choices.note: Free; it ends in a fortnight either way

events.text: The student newspaper has asked for funding, an office, and an undertaking that the college will not read it before it is printed. The editor is nineteen and has put the three requests in that order on purpose.

choices.label: Fund it and give the undertaking
Give them the room, not the money
Decline all three
choices.note: Free; it will be printed anyway

events.text: The housing lottery has been run twice because the first run put eleven students in rooms that do not exist. The Dean of Students has proposed, in writing, that the college stop calling it a lottery.

choices.label: Lease rooms in town for the year

events.text: A petition about the dining hall has reached eleven hundred signatures, which is more students than {school} has. The kitchen's position is that it is doing what the contract says, and the kitchen is right.

choices.label: Buy out the contract and start again
Put students on the catering committee

events.text: Rag Week has raised nine thousand dollars for the county hospital. It has also moved a caravan onto the roof of {building}, and produced a bill for the crane that will be needed to take it off again.

choices.label: Pay for the crane and say nothing
Bill the students’ union
choices.note: Free; the caravan stays a while

events.text: The college has never settled on a mascot. The students have settled on one: a heron, which lives on the pond and has bitten two people. The Athletics Director has produced a costume without being asked.

choices.label: Refer it to a committee
choices.note: Free; the heron wins in the end

events.text: A paper has got out ahead of the examination. Eleven students are known to have seen it; the number who saw it and said nothing is not known and cannot be. The Proctor has asked for a decision before Friday.

choices.label: Void the paper and resit the whole cohort

events.text: Something is going round the residences. The Health Centre has seen ninety students in four days and has run out of the only thing that helps, which is a room to put them in that is not the room they share.

choices.label: Take rooms in town and staff them
Let it run its course
choices.note: Free; a fortnight of teaching goes

events.text: The Development Office would like to run a proper telephone campaign: students calling alumni in the evenings, a script, a target. The last one raised four times what it cost and was described in two letters as 'undignified'.

choices.label: Leave the ledger alone this year

events.text: The {class} have written collectively. The letter is careful, signed by nineteen of them, and concerns a building that is not there any more, a tradition that has lapsed, and the fact that nobody told them about either.

choices.label: Answer it properly and invite them back

events.text: The alumni would like a seat on the board, filled by election rather than by invitation. They have been polite about it for six years and have now been polite about it in a letter with four hundred names attached.

choices.label: Create the seat
choices.note: Free; the board is one vote less predictable

events.text: A donor will fund the shortfall outright, in exchange for the name of {building}. It currently carries the name of a former president, about whom nobody has asked anything in some years.

choices.label: Take the gift and change the name
choices.note: $2.5M; the old name goes to a corridor

events.text: The deposits are behind. The Dean of Admissions has proposed a second round of offers, which works, and has also proposed not describing it as a second round, which is where the conversation slowed down.

choices.label: Go to a second round
choices.note: The class fills; it is weaker

choices.label: Hold the line and take a smaller class

events.text: A parent has written about the fee. The letter is four pages, entirely reasonable, encloses a photocopy of the prospectus from the year their eldest started, and ends by asking what exactly has been added since.

choices.label: Fund more aid and say so publicly
Send the figures and an explanation

events.text: {school} has appeared in a guidebook for the first time. The entry is three sentences long, broadly accurate, and describes the campus as 'pleasant if underfunded', which the board has read in two entirely different tones.

choices.label: Buy the larger entry next year

events.text: Admissions would like to visit schools in three states rather than one. The case is a page long and rests on a single sentence: nobody who has not heard of {school} has applied to it.

events.title: The fire
events.text:
The fire began in a service riser in {building} at some time after two in the morning and was out by six. Nobody was in the building. The night porter, who was, walked the whole of the upper floor before the brigade arrived and would like it recorded that he was following the procedure, which he was not.

What is lost is the east end: three teaching rooms, the departmental office and forty years of a filing system nobody had photographed. The insurers will meet part of it. Their assessor has used the phrase 'deferred maintenance' twice in a preliminary note and will use it again.

The Dean would like to know what to tell the students who had lectures there on Monday, and has asked in a way that suggests the answer matters more than the building does.

choices.label: Rebuild the east end as it was
Replace it with something cheaper and newer
Close the east end and manage without it

events.title: The matter in the Bursary
events.text:
The irregularity in the Bursary accounts is eleven years old, amounts to rather more than was first thought, and was found by a temporary clerk checking something else. The person responsible retired four years ago with a presentation and a speech.

The auditors have been informed because they had to be. The board has been informed because the auditors informed them. The press have not been informed, yet, and the Communications Officer has written the word 'yet' on the briefing note in a hand that suggests she does not expect that to last.

There is a version of this where {school} announces it first, plainly, with the figure and the referral, and takes a bad fortnight. There is a version where it does not, and the fortnight arrives anyway, later, with the college having chosen its own silence to explain.

choices.label: Announce it, refer it, and publish the figure
Handle it internally and recover what can be recovered
Close the file and change the procedure

events.title: The Whitfield bequest
events.text:
Eleanor Whitfield left {school} almost everything, which is a great deal more than anyone expected, and a letter of three sentences explaining why. She graduated in a year the college would rather not dwell on, was taught by two people it has since named rooms after, and gave nothing at all for forty years.

The letter says she did not give before because nobody asked her anything except for money. It says she is giving now because of a conversation with a student caller who asked what she had studied and then asked a second question about it. It does not name the student.

The executors are ready. The board has met twice already and has not agreed, because a sum this size is not a gift to a college so much as a decision about what the college is going to be.

choices.label: Endow it and spend only the income
Build with it now
choices.note: Buildings the students here will use

choices.label: Clear the debt and steady the ship

events.title: The occupation
events.text:
The administration building has been occupied since Thursday. It is orderly: there is a rota, the post is being passed through, and somebody has been watering the plants in the outer office. The demands run to two pages and are mostly about money, which is to say mostly about things the college has already conceded it cannot afford.

The faculty are divided in a way that is new. Eleven have signed a letter supporting the students. Three have signed one opposing it. The rest are waiting to see which letter it is better to have signed, which is the part the President has found most instructive.

The town is watching. The board is waiting. The students in the building are, on the whole, being more reasonable than anyone outside it.

choices.label: Negotiate in public and concede what is true
Wait, and keep talking
choices.note: Free; it ends by itself in a month

choices.label: End the occupation
choices.note: Free, and remembered for thirty years

events.text: A prospective student's parent has telephoned to ask whether {school} is accredited, which it is, and how long it has been going, which is the part the Registrar found harder to answer warmly. Nobody in the county has heard of the place yet.

choices.label: Let the first graduates be the advertisement

events.text: The operating account has more in it than the college has ever held and no plan attached to any of it. Three memos have arrived this week proposing uses. The Bursar has pointed out, with feeling, that money sitting still is the only kind that is certainly not doing anything.

choices.label: Spend it on the students who are here now
Hold it against a bad year

events.text: The endowment is smaller than it was ten years ago and smaller than the comparator colleges the board keeps a table of. The table is not in the papers this time, which everyone has noticed.

choices.label: Stop drawing and let it recover
Leave it
choices.note: Free; the table returns next year

events.text: Salaries are now most of what the college spends. The Bursar's paper says this plainly in one line and then spends four pages explaining that it is not, in itself, a criticism of anybody, which is how everyone knows what the paper is about.

choices.label: Hold salaries for a year
choices.note: Saves it; they read the paper too

choices.label: Grow the rest of the college instead

events.text: The photographs for the prospectus have come back and the Admissions Office would like to discuss them. The buildings are all present and correct. The difficulty is what is between them, which in most of the frames is nothing at all.

Something is going right. The returns are good, the leavers are few, and three students have written to the President unprompted, which has not happened before. The Dean would like to know what the college is doing, so that it can keep doing it.

choices.label: Put money behind whatever it is
Write it down and carry on

events.text: It has been a long few terms. Nothing single has gone badly enough to write about, and the accumulation of it is in the corridors, in the returns, and in the number of people who have stopped coming to things.

choices.label: Say nothing and let it pass

events.text: The timetable for next term has been drawn up and shows the same three names against every hour of it. It is workable. The Registrar has attached a note observing that it is workable only for as long as none of the three is ill.

The central boiler, installed in the college's first decade, has begun to make a noise the facilities director describes in writing as 'a sort of cough'. It is still producing heat. The facilities director would like it noted that he said so first.

choices.label: Nurse it through the winter
choices.note: $250k a winter, and it will cough again

choices.label: Defer it to the summer works
choices.note: Free now; the backlog carries it

events.text: The walk from the residence halls to the dining hall froze overnight into a single continuous sheet, and was crossed at breakfast by most of the first year in a manner facilities describes as 'improvised'. Nobody is badly hurt. One wrist.

choices.label: Hire a second gritting crew
choices.note: $80k; the walk is a walk again

events.text: The heating bill for December has arrived. It is larger than November's by a figure the bursar has circled, and then, in a different pen, circled again.

choices.label: Turn every thermostat down two degrees

events.text: It snowed eleven inches overnight. The registrar would like a decision on whether today's classes are cancelled. The students, on the evidence of the main lawn, have already made one.

choices.label: Declare a snow day
choices.note: The lawn is a battlefield by ten

choices.label: Hold classes
choices.note: The teaching goes on; so does the grumbling

events.text: The spring term has started in the dark: sunrise after the first lecture, sunset before the last. The counselling service has asked, in a memo with a sun drawn on it, for a daylight lamp in every common room.
The snow on the flat roofs is now deep enough that the structural engineer has asked, politely and in writing, for it to be somewhere else. He has attached a diagram with arrows on it.

choices.label: Wait for the thaw
choices.note: Free now; the membranes will not forget

events.title: The freeze
events.text:
The coldest night in forty years came on the Sunday before term, and on the Monday the pipes gave way in three buildings at once. Water came through the ceiling of a lecture theatre in the kind of steady, reasonable way that suggests it has been planning this. The porters worked through the night and saved the rare books by carrying them, one trolley at a time, to the only room in the college that was still dry, which was the chaplain's.

The insurers have sent a man. He has a clipboard and a very good coat.

choices.label: Start the term a week late

events.text: The {sport} team has won the title, and the campus has not slept since. The boosters would like a parade down the main walk, the athletics director would like a new scoreboard, and the provost would like to know when anyone intends to go back to class.

choices.label: Hold the parade
choices.note: $80k and a day off; the students remember it

choices.label: Let the boosters pay for the scoreboard
choices.note: Their money, their name on it

choices.label: A reception and back to work

events.title: The recruiting file
events.text:
A reporter has the {sport} programme's recruiting file, and in it a series of payments to the families of players, routed through a booster's landscaping business. The coach says he knew nothing. The booster says the coach knew everything. The league's compliance office has asked for the college's response by the end of the month.

The college can report itself and take what comes, fight it, or settle quietly and hope the reporter moves on.

choices.label: Report the college and fire the coach
choices.note: $200k in fines; the board respects it

choices.label: Fight it
choices.note: $600k in lawyers, and the story runs for a year

choices.label: Settle quietly
choices.note: $300k; the alumni hear about it anyway

events.text: Students from {rival} broke into the bell tower overnight — or the tallest building, in its absence — and hung their colours from the top. The Dean of Students has a list of names, a photograph of the banner, and a request from our own students to be allowed to answer in kind.

choices.label: Look the other way while they answer
choices.note: The students are delighted; their president writes a letter

choices.label: Challenge them to a charity match
choices.note: Good press, and a cheque for the food bank

events.text: The board chair has brought the guide to the meeting, open at the table, with the college's line underlined twice. She would like to know what the administration intends to do about it, and has a consultant in mind.

choices.label: Hire the consultant
choices.note: $250k for a report on the report

choices.label: Explain the methodology to the board
Promise a rise within five years

events.text: A regional bank would like to put its name on the college's playing fields — the whole of them, and the scoreboard, and the tickets — for a gift that would pay the athletics budget for a decade. The students' paper has already drafted the editorial.

choices.label: Take the name and the money
choices.note: $2M to the endowment; the students notice

events.text: {suitor} has offered {faculty} a named chair and a laboratory twice the size of the one they have. They would rather stay, they say, but they would like to be asked.

choices.label: Match the offer
choices.note: Their salary rises by a quarter, for good

choices.label: Wish them well
choices.note: They go, and the college that took them is more of a rival for it

events.text: The neighbours have written again about Thursday nights: the music, the singing on the walk home, and a traffic cone now on the roof of their garage. They would like a meeting, and they have copied the local paper.

choices.label: Impose quiet hours
choices.note: The neighbours are mollified; the students are not

choices.label: Meet the neighbours and send a gift

events.text: The reading rooms were full at four in the morning for the third week running, and the college nurse has seen more exhaustion this term than flu. The student paper has a front page about it and a list of demands.

choices.label: Close the reading rooms at midnight

events.text: A national foundation has funded a centre proposal from {faculty}, and the overhead on the grant is more than the department's budget. The foundation would like to know where the centre will be housed.

choices.label: Find the centre a home
choices.note: $300k of fitting out; the overhead is the college's

choices.label: Let it go to a partner college

events.text: A trustee's grandson has applied, and his file is not strong. The trustee has not mentioned it, which is how everyone knows he would like it mentioned.

choices.label: Admit him
choices.note: The trustee is grateful; the admissions office is not

choices.label: Treat the file like any other
choices.note: The trustee is quiet at the next meeting

events.title: The protest
events.text:
They came back for it: three generations of alumni, a string quartet, and a banner with {building} painted on it the way it looked the year they arrived. They stood on the rubble in their reunion scarves and read the names of everyone who ever taught in it. The student paper's front page is a photograph of the last wall coming down.

The board would like a statement. The alumni would like more than that.

choices.label: Promise a memorial where it stood
choices.note: $300k, and a plaque the alumni can visit

choices.label: Give its name to what replaces it
choices.note: The board approves; the alumni are half-mollified

events.text: Facilities has issued three hundred and forty permits for a car park with two hundred and twelve spaces, on the reasoning that not everyone comes in at once. On the second Monday of term everyone came in at once.

choices.label: Lay out a second car park

events.text: A pipe above the second floor of {building} burst on the Saturday and ran until Monday, when the first seminar of the week found it. The ceiling tiles are drying in the corridor, stacked and numbered by somebody from the porters' lodge, which Facilities describes as the most useful thing done all weekend.

choices.label: Replace the whole run of pipe
choices.note: $220k; the rest of it was the same age

choices.label: Repair the burst and dry it out
choices.note: $18k; the rest of the run is the same age, and everybody knows it

events.text: Somebody has painted a fox on the end wall of {building} overnight: nine feet tall, anatomically careful, and rather good. Grounds are ready with the pressure washer. The art department has asked them to wait until it has been photographed, and then, on reflection, to wait a little longer.

choices.label: Have it cleaned off
choices.note: $8k; the wall is a wall again

choices.label: Leave the fox where it is
choices.note: Free; the board will ask about it

choices.label: Commission a proper mural beside it

events.text: The master key to {building} has been lost. It was last seen on a ring with nine others and a small plastic lobster, and the locksmith's estimate for changing every lock in the building runs to four pages.

choices.label: Change every lock in the building
Move the whole campus to key cards
Keep looking for it
choices.note: Free; whoever has it still has it

events.text: Rain has been getting into {building} along the valley gutter, and there are now nine buckets in the top-floor corridor. The porters empty them twice a day and have begun logging the volumes in a notebook, which they would like someone senior to read, because the numbers are going up.

The lift in {building} has stopped between floors for the fourth time this term, most recently for fifty minutes with the Dean inside it. The Dean used the time to draft a memo about the lift, which has now arrived, and which notes that for some students the stairs are not an alternative.

choices.label: Service it and post a notice

events.text: The county's heritage officer would like to list {building} as a building of special interest. Listing would protect it from alteration of any kind, and the officer has confirmed, when asked a second time, that this includes the repairs.

choices.label: Support the listing
choices.note: Free; every repair now needs consent

choices.label: Object to the listing
choices.note: $30k in advice; the alumni hear of it

events.text: Two senior members of {program} have not spoken for six years, since a disagreement over a footnote that neither of them now cites. The department has arranged for them to attend alternate meetings, and has asked, as a practical matter, whether a second photocopier might help.

choices.label: Split the department in two
choices.note: $60k a year for a second office

events.text: The new timetable has put the required methods course for {program} in the same hour as the only other course the program requires. Forty students cannot graduate on time without being in two rooms at once. The Registrar's office says the software did it, and the software has not commented.

choices.label: Redraw the timetable
choices.note: $25k and a fortnight of the Registrar

choices.label: Run an extra section in the evening

events.text: The plagiarism software licensed last year has flagged two first-year essays in five. One of them is an essay on academic honesty, flagged for quoting the college's own policy, correctly and with a citation.

choices.label: Review every flagged case by hand
Cancel the licence
choices.note: Saves $20k; the real cases go unflagged

choices.label: Let the flags stand
choices.note: Free; forty hearings, and letters home

events.text: The Curriculum Committee has met eleven times on whether first-years should take a writing course, and has approved the minutes of all eleven meetings and nothing else. The chair has asked whether the President might 'indicate a view', in a tone that suggests a request to be rescued.

choices.label: Leave it with the committee
choices.note: Free; the twelfth meeting is booked

events.text: The median grade has risen for the ninth year running and now sits a short way below the top of the scale. A graduate school has written to ask what an A from {school} is meant to signify, in a tone that suggests it has already formed a view.

choices.label: Print the median beside every grade
choices.note: Free; the students read their own transcripts

choices.label: Leave the grades alone
choices.note: Free; the next letter will be less polite

events.text: The safety inspector has been through the laboratories and found a fume cupboard last certified the year it was installed, a fridge marked NO FOOD with somebody's lunch in it, and an eyewash station connected to nothing. The report is polite, numbered, and gives the college twenty-eight days.

choices.label: Put everything on the list right
Fix the fume cupboard and the eyewash
choices.note: $55k; the rest waits for the reinspection

choices.label: Close the laboratories until it is done
choices.note: Free; a term of practicals lost

events.text: The longest-serving teacher in {program} retires in June, after enough years that two of the current department were once her students. The department would like a dinner, a volume of essays, and her office kept exactly as it is for a year, and has listed these in ascending order of seriousness.

choices.label: Hold the dinner and fund the volume
Endow a prize in her name
Send a card and reallocate the office

events.text: It is exam season and the library closes at midnight. At ten past, most nights, a porter walks the stacks with a torch and finds thirty or forty students who did not hear the bell, are very sorry, and would like five more minutes.

choices.label: Open the library all night in exams
Keep to midnight closing
choices.note: Free; the porter keeps his torch

events.text: The laundry room in the residence halls has six machines, two of which work, and one of which works only if struck in a place the students have marked with tape. A rota has appeared on the door. It is fairer than anything the college has issued this year.

choices.label: Repair the two that can be repaired

events.text: The dining hall added a vegan dish to the lunch counter this term, and it has sold out by half past twelve every day since. The catering manager would like to know whether the college intends to plan for this, or to go on being surprised by it at half past twelve.

choices.label: Expand the menu and retrain the kitchen
Make Mondays meat-free across the hall
Keep it to a single dish
choices.note: Free; it sells out at half past twelve

events.text: A cat has moved into the porters' lodge. It arrived in October, has been fed by at least four people who each believed they were the only one, and now appears in more student photographs than the President does.

choices.label: Adopt the cat on the college's books
choices.note: $2k in vet's bills and a collar

choices.label: Find it a home in town
Leave the arrangement as it is
choices.note: Free; the insurers ask one question

events.text: Forty-one bicycles have been stolen from outside {building} since the start of term. Campus security describes it as a wave. The insurer has declined to describe it as anything until it has seen the locks, and the students' union has begun selling better ones at cost.

choices.label: Install covered, lit racks with cameras

events.text: Six students have been on hunger strike for eleven days on the steps of {building}, asking the college to publish where the endowment is invested. They are taking water and seeing the nurse each morning. The nurse has written to say that the second week is when it stops being a gesture.

choices.label: Publish the holdings and meet them
choices.note: $60k in advisers' fees; the strike ends

choices.label: Meet them and explain the policy
choices.note: Free; it may not be enough

events.text: Orientation went wrong in its first hour, when the coaches meeting the new students at the station took them to a college with a similar name forty miles away. The other college gave them lunch and a tour, and has written, generously, to say that several of them asked about transferring.

choices.label: Fetch them and restart the week properly
choices.note: $30k; a day late and a good week

choices.label: Carry on with the programme as printed
choices.note: Free; they arrive for the second half

events.text: A student society has invited a speaker whose views half the campus finds objectionable and the other half has not yet looked up. The society has booked the largest lecture room, two other societies have booked the corridor outside it, and Security would like a decision by Wednesday.

choices.label: Let it go ahead and pay for security
Add a reply session straight after
Cancel it on safety grounds
choices.note: Free; the society writes to the paper

events.text: A donor has offered $1.5M towards the scholarship fund, on condition that a bronze of himself be placed at the main entrance. The sculptor has already been engaged, and the maquette shows him somewhat taller than the Registrar remembers.

choices.label: Accept the gift and the statue
choices.note: $1.5M to the endowment; the students name it within a week

choices.label: Offer a named scholarship instead
choices.note: $600k, if he agrees; a plaque, not a plinth

choices.label: Decline the gift
choices.note: Nothing, and a very long letter in reply

events.text: The {class} has raised a reunion gift and would like it spent on a clock for the main walk, with the class year on its face. The committee has chosen the clock, the typeface, and the year, which is off by one.

choices.label: Install the clock as given
choices.note: $250k from the class; the error is cast in iron

choices.label: Ask them to fund bursaries instead
choices.note: $250k to the endowment; some of them come round

events.text: An alumnus has given the college a racehorse, with papers, a trainer, and a stable bill already running. The horse has won twice in four starts, and the Development Office would like it minuted that it did not ask for this.

choices.label: Sell the horse at auction
choices.note: $140k, and a photograph for the annual report

choices.label: Race it for a season in the college colours
choices.note: $60k in fees; the students follow every start

events.text: The honorary degrees committee has put forward a shipping magnate whose foundation has been generous and whose company is currently in court on three continents. The committee's paper describes this as 'a matter for the courts', twice.

choices.label: Confer the degree
choices.note: A gift of $500k is understood; the student paper is less understanding

choices.label: Withdraw the nomination
choices.note: Free; the committee is embarrassed and the students approve

events.text: An audit of the alumni records has found that a third of the addresses are out of date and eleven belong to the same house. The house has been receiving the annual appeal in bulk since before its current owners bought it.

choices.label: Hire an alumni records officer
choices.note: $55k a year; the appeal starts arriving

choices.label: Pay students to clean it over the summer
Leave the records as they are
choices.note: Free; the house keeps the letters

events.text: A trustee has offered to match every alumni gift dollar for dollar up to $1M, if the challenge is announced and a fifth of the alumni give. She has chosen the fifth deliberately and has not said why.

choices.label: Announce the challenge and campaign for it
choices.note: $90k in mailing and calls; about $1.6M if it lands

choices.label: Ask her for a smaller gift, no conditions

events.text: The students have petitioned the investment committee to divest from the companies named in a nineteen-page appendix. The committee has read the appendix, found two of its own holdings, and one of its own members' employers.

choices.label: Divest from the named holdings
choices.note: About $1.2M off the endowment in fees and missed returns

choices.label: Commission a review of the policy
Hold the portfolio as it is
choices.note: Free; the petition becomes an encampment on the lawn

events.text: The insurers have renewed the property policy at a premium forty per cent higher than last year. Their surveyor's letter lists fourteen items of concern, the ninth of which is described only as 'the smell'.

choices.label: Fix the list and ask for a re-survey
choices.note: $450k off the backlog; the premium holds

events.text: The auditors have found a bank account in the college's name that nobody in the Bursar's office remembers opening. It holds $38k and a standing order, still running, to a florist.

choices.label: Close the account and bring it on the books
choices.note: $38k back, and a note in the management letter

choices.label: Hire a controller to find the others
choices.note: $95k a year; the board sleeps better

events.text: The three-yearly valuation of the staff pension scheme shows a shortfall. The actuary's letter is courteous, and it says the gap will grow if nothing is done.

choices.label: Raise contributions over time
choices.note: $70k a year on the faculty payroll

choices.label: Wait for the next valuation
choices.note: Free; the staff read the letter too

events.text: A drinks company has offered the college an exclusive pouring contract: its machines in every building, its logo on the scoreboard, its colour on the recycling bins. The draft runs to forty pages, three of which concern the bins.

choices.label: Sign the contract
choices.note: $350k up front; the students lose the other brand

events.text: A developer has offered to buy the wooded strip along the college's northern edge, which the college has owned since its founding and has never once found a use for. The offer letter refers to it as 'the opportunity site'.

choices.label: Sell the strip
choices.note: $2.5M; the trees come down in spring

choices.label: Lease it for twenty years
choices.note: $300k now; the trees stay, for now

choices.label: Keep the land
choices.note: Free; the board asks what it is for

events.text: The board has asked for a strategic plan. The last one is in the President's filing cabinet, in a binder whose spine reads 'Vision', and nobody has opened it since the year it was printed.

choices.label: Write it in-house over the summer
Reissue the old plan with new dates
choices.note: Free; one trustee has kept a copy

events.text: The lowest bid for the new roofing contract has come from a firm owned by the brother-in-law of the chair of the buildings committee. The chair has declared the interest, recused himself, and asked how the vote went.

choices.label: Award it to the lowest bid

events.text: The consultants have delivered their report, two hundred and twelve pages, and its central finding is that the college should 'lean into its distinctiveness'. The appendix describing the distinctiveness appears to have been written for a previous client.

choices.label: Implement the recommendations
choices.note: $80k a year for an Office of Distinctiveness

choices.label: Adopt the executive summary only
choices.note: Free; the board likes the summary

choices.label: Thank the consultants and shelve it
choices.note: Free; the fee is spent either way

events.text: The board would like the President's residence refurbished before the trustees' dinner. The proposal includes a wine room, a second dining room, and a line item headed 'dignity', which is the largest.

choices.label: Decline the refurbishment
choices.note: Free; the dinner is held in the old dining room

events.text: The secretary to the board is retiring after thirty-one years. The minutes of every meeting since the founding are in her handwriting, and in a shorthand of her own devising that no one else can read.

choices.label: Appoint a full-time successor
choices.note: $70k a year; the minutes are typed

choices.label: Pay her to transcribe the archive first
Rotate the minutes among the trustees

events.text: A governance review has recommended term limits for trustees. The longest-serving trustee has been on the board for twenty-six years, chaired the committee that commissioned the review, and would like to discuss the transition arrangements.

choices.label: Adopt term limits
choices.note: Free; three seats open over two years

choices.label: Adopt them for new trustees only

events.text: The guide's reputation survey has arrived, asking the President to rate twenty-four other colleges from one to five. Last year's return rated {rival} a two, and the President's office would like to know whether that is still the college's position.

choices.label: Send every president a glossy brochure first
Fill it in honestly and send it back
Leave it in the in-tray
choices.note: Free; the guide counts the silence

events.text: A promotional film made by {rival} has been watched more times than {rival} has living alumni. It features a rowing eight at dawn, a lecture in a meadow, and a golden retriever that does not appear to be enrolled.

choices.label: Commission a film of our own
Let the film society make one
Let it pass
choices.note: Free; the admissions office watches it anyway

events.text: {rival} has offered the {sport} coach a head job, a car, and a salary the athletics budget has never contemplated. The coach has told the team, the team has told the student paper, and the paper has run it above the fold.

choices.label: Let the coach go with thanks

events.text: The booster club has offered $300k for the {sport} programme, with one request attached: a seat on the committee that appoints the coach. The club's president has put the request in the covering letter and the cheque in the same envelope.

choices.label: Accept the gift and the seat
Take the money, decline the seat
choices.note: $150k, if they agree; about half do

events.title: The river
events.text:
The river came over the east meadow on the Thursday and did not stop at the path, which the planning documents had assured everyone it would. By the Saturday there was water to the second step of {building} and a canoe tied to the bicycle racks, and the grounds staff had carried the ground-floor archive up a storey by hand, box by box, through the night.

Nobody was hurt. The loss adjuster has described the damage as 'general', which the Clerk of Works has asked him to define. The hydrologist whose report the board received and noted some years ago has written to say she is sorry to have been right.

choices.label: Move teaching off the ground floors

events.title: The sickness term
events.text:
The first cases came in the week after the autumn break, and by the end of the month a quarter of the college had been ill at once. The public health office has not ordered anything, and has said so in a letter that reads very much like a request. Lectures are running at half attendance, the kitchens are sending trays to the residences, and the chaplain has been sitting up with the students who are frightened, who are more numerous than the ones who are seriously sick.

The question in front of the college is whether to finish the term in person, finish it at a distance, or end it early and examine in the spring.

choices.label: End the term early and examine in spring
Teach at a distance until it passes
Keep the college open as normal
choices.note: Free; the case count is published weekly

events.title: The essay ring
events.text:
An external examiner in {program} noticed that four dissertations shared a bibliography, down to the same misspelled author. The inquiry that followed has found a paid essay service run from a flat off campus, a customer list of a hundred and forty names, and a price list the Academic Registrar describes as 'competitive'. Some of the names have already graduated.

Most of the students on the list were frightened of failing, and the Dean of Students would like that to count. The Senate would like the degrees to mean what they say. Both are right, which is why it has come to the President.

choices.label: Rescind the degrees and fail the rest
choices.note: $300k in appeals; the degrees mean it

choices.label: Require resits and note it on the record
Close the service and move on
choices.note: Free; the list stays in a drawer

events.title: The state grant
events.text:
The legislature has closed the tuition grant scheme at the end of a budget session that ran into the small hours. The letter informing {school} arrived eleven days after the vote, is a page and a half long, and describes the change as a 'transition'. Roughly one student in six held one of the grants.

The families affected have begun telephoning the Financial Aid office, which has three staff and has stopped taking lunch. The college can replace the money, some of it, or none of it, and each answer has names attached.

choices.label: Replace the grants in full
choices.note: $2.8M this year; nobody leaves for money

choices.label: Replace them for students already enrolled
Let the grants lapse
choices.note: Free; about fifty students do not come back

events.title: The Harrowgate pledge
events.text:
Harrowgate & Sons has gone into administration owing more than anyone outside the firm had guessed, and with it has gone the second half of Arthur Harrowgate's pledge to {school}. The first half is spent. It is in the foundations of a building that already has his name cut into the lintel in letters eleven inches high.

The administrators have written to ask whether the college regards the money received so far as a gift or as an asset of the estate, and have enclosed a form. Mr Harrowgate has written separately, by hand, to apologise.

choices.label: Finish the building from the endowment
choices.note: $3M from the fund; the name stays

choices.label: Contest the administrators' claim
choices.note: $500k in lawyers to keep what was given

choices.label: Mothball the unfinished wing
choices.note: $250k to make safe; the backlog carries it

events.title: The prospectus case
events.text:
Thirty-one graduates of {program} have filed suit over a line in the prospectus that promised 'employment in the field within six months' and gave a percentage. The percentage came from a survey of nine people, four of whom were related to the member of staff who conducted it. The line was withdrawn eight years ago, but not before it had been printed forty thousand times.

Counsel's advice runs to twenty pages and concludes that the college would probably win, eventually, at a cost. The graduates' own letter is two pages long and does not mention money until the last paragraph.

choices.label: Defend the case
choices.note: $700k in fees, and two years in the papers

choices.label: Offer them further study without fees

events.title: The loss
events.text:
A second-year student died on the Sunday night. The coroner has not yet reported, and the college has said nothing beyond confirming it, at the family's request. Her friends have spent most of the week together in the common room, and the staff who taught her have been in and out of the Dean's office in a way the Dean has not tried to schedule.

The student paper has asked, carefully, whether the college's support was adequate. The honest answer is that the counselling service is two people with a six-week waiting list. Her parents have asked the same question in a letter that deserves a better answer than that.

choices.label: Fund a proper counselling service
choices.note: $250k a year, for good; the waiting list goes

choices.label: Hold a memorial and change nothing

events.title: The kitchens
events.text:
The dining hall staff walked out at six on Monday morning, forty-two of them, after the third year running in which their pay was held and the faculty's was not. They are outside the service entrance with a brazier and a hand-lettered sign, and the students who stop to talk are given tea from a flask. Nobody inside has made a breakfast since.

The students are eating from the vending machines and the town's two takeaways, and a petition in support of the staff has been signed by more of them than voted in the last union election. The claim itself is modest. The precedent it sets for every other line of the payroll is not, which is the point the Bursar has made twice.

choices.label: Meet the claim in full
choices.note: $180k a year, for good; the kitchens reopen

choices.label: Offer a one-off payment and a review
Bring in a catering contractor
choices.note: $150k to end it; nobody forgets how

events.title: The records
events.text:
Someone has copied the Registry's database: names, addresses, transcripts and the financial aid files of every student since the founding. The college learned of it from a message to the Registrar's inbox with a sample attached and a sum in a currency nobody in the building had heard of. The IT office is four people and a contractor, and the contractor has explained that the server in question was on the list to be replaced.

The alumni affected are all of them. None has been told yet, and how they are told will be remembered longer than the breach itself.

choices.label: Tell everyone and pay for protection
Notify only those the law requires
Pay the demand
choices.note: $800k, and no guarantee it is the end

events.title: The hole
events.text:
A hole eleven metres across opened overnight beside {building}, taking with it a bench, a length of path and a sundial that a founding benefactor gave and nobody could read. The geologists say the ground beneath the older half of the campus is limestone that has been dissolving quietly for some time, and that there are probably others. They have marked three more places with orange paint.

The building is standing, and the engineers would like it kept empty until they have drilled. The hole has been photographed from the cordon at all hours, which the Communications Office has decided to regard as engagement.

choices.label: Survey and grout the whole campus
Fill this one and watch the others

events.title: The name on the prize
events.text:
The most famous graduate of the {class}, and of the college's publicity for a generation, has been convicted of a fraud large enough to have its own documentary in preparation. His name is on the annual prize for leadership, a seminar room and the back page of the alumni magazine, where he appears shaking hands with three successive presidents. The prize was last awarded a month ago.

The people he defrauded include a pension fund and several hundred households. A number of alumni have written asking for his name to come down. A smaller number have written to say that {school} does not rewrite its history, and the largest donor among them has copied in the board.

choices.label: Take his name down everywhere
choices.note: $150k in signage, and a $1.5M gift withdrawn

choices.label: Give his gifts to the victims' fund
choices.note: $2M from the endowment; the name goes with it

choices.label: Keep the name and issue a statement

events.title: The merger proposal
events.text:
{rival} has written proposing a merger. The letter is courteous and long, and its appendix lists the savings to be had from one registry, one catalogue and one set of sports grounds, most of which would be theirs. The name of the combined institution is left blank, in a way that suggests it has been discussed.

The board received a copy directly, which is how the President learned the letter existed. Two trustees think it is the best offer the college will ever have. The rest would like to know why {rival} thinks the college needs one.

choices.label: Decline it publicly
choices.note: Free; the rivalry is louder for it

choices.label: Open talks on shared services
choices.note: $1.8M saved; some staff are shared out of a job

choices.label: Enter merger negotiations
choices.note: $2.5M in transition funds; the name is on the table

readings.pending: What the world is asking you about now. An inline event waits a few weeks and then resolves itself the way the ticker says it will.
readings.mood: How the last few events have left the students feeling; it fades over a year or two.
readings.history: Every event this run and what was chosen.
